extracted.intended_audience: USPTO leadership, supervisors, OPQA staff, policymakers, oversight bodies, and patent quality stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for measuring and improving the quality of patent examination at the USPTO, including OPQA review practices, the composite quality metric components, supervisory data collection, signatory authority reviews, and detection/discipline for work-credit abuses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Disposition Compliance Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Percent of final decisions without errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Component 1 of USPTO’s composite quality metric; weight = 20%. Based on OPQA reviews of final decisions and contributes to corps-wide accuracy rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-process Compliance Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Percent of preliminary (in-process) decisions without errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Component 2 of the composite quality metric; weight = 15%. Based on OPQA reviews of preliminary decisions and influences the official accuracy metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Action on the Merits Search Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Score given for the quality of the patent examiners’ initial search for related technology (prior art).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Component 3 of the composite quality metric; weight = 10%. Assesses the thoroughness and appropriateness of the examiner’s prior art search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete First Action on the Merits Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Score given for the degree to which the preliminary decision conforms to USPTO best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Component 4 of the composite quality metric; weight = 10%. Evaluates conformity of the first action to established examination procedures and best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Index Report (QIR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical representation of different quality-related issues during the patent examination process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Component 5 of the composite quality metric; weight = 20%. QIR data is derived from PALM and includes events such as how often applications are reopened after an examiner closes review and the number of determinations made on an application. Useful for identifying examiners whose behavior deviates from peers, but does not by itself explain underlying causes of errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: External Quality Survey
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey that measures quality concerns expressed by patent attorneys and applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Component 6 of the composite quality metric; weight = 15%. Captures applicant/attorney perceptions of USPTO examination quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal Quality Survey
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey that measures quality concerns expressed by USPTO’s patent examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Component 7 of the composite quality metric; weight = 10%. Captures examiner-reported quality concerns and perceptions within the corps.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPQA error definition and classification (clear errors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors are defined as unreasonable failures by the patent examiner to reject patent claims for one or more reasons provided in the patent laws, or when an examiner incorrectly rejects patent claims (known internally as clear errors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPQA records why a determination had an error and which area of patent law the examiner did not follow. These error identifications feed components 1 and 2 of the composite metric. Accurate and consistent error classification is critical because OPQA-derived inputs heavily influence corps-wide accuracy rates and supervisor bonuses.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPQA sampling scope and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: OPQA independently reviews a random statistical sample of examiner determinations (on average less than 1% of all office actions annually).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPQA’s stated role is to generate statistically significant corps-wide estimates of accuracy, not to catch or prevent every low-quality patent. Because sampling is small (<1%), OPQA’s procedures, consistency, and how errors are recorded materially affect the official quality metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace period for new patent examination guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice of allowing examiners a 6- to 12-month grace period after USPTO issues new examination guidance before OPQA charges applicable errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the grace period OPQA may flag decisions as 'Needs Attention' rather than recording an official error. This practice is not in written SOP, is applied inconsistently (some reviewers wait 6 months, others 12), and reduces confidence in the official quality metric because components 1 and 2 (which together comprise 35% of the composite) depend on recorded errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and meaning of 'Needs Attention' flag
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Needs Attention' is applied by OPQA reviewers in lieu of an official error to identify issues that may not rise to an error (e.g., unchecked form fields, issues covered by the new-guidance grace period, or instances of exceptional examination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'Needs Attention' label is not an official error and Technology Centers are not required to respond to it; its rising use (from ~15% in FY2009 to ~21% in recent years) may mask true error rates and reduce Technology Center awareness and corrective action for errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording and categorization of errors by OPQA reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: OPQA reviewers have reported identifying but not always recording errors; some errors are ignored or flagged only as 'Needs Attention'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No written policy governs this practice; inconsistency in recording errors (and delayed charging after new guidance) can underrepresent the true error rate and distort composite quality metrics. Written policies and consistent standards for when to record errors are recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPQA internal audit and SOP completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: OPQA follows ISO quality management standards and conducts internal audits against its SOP, but not all procedures are included in the SOP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit procedures that only test documented SOP steps will miss informal/unwritten practices (e.g., the grace period, recusal procedures). Audits are sometimes predictable and thus may not effectively detect noncompliance or informal practices. Recommendations include expanding SOP content and varying audit processes to detect informal behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervisory data collection in the SPE Management Database (SMD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supervisors should record performance ratings, bonuses, signatory review cases, and errors in SMD; USPTO mandated recording supervisor-found errors in April 2014.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before the mandate supervisors did not consistently record errors or which cases they reviewed, preventing analysis of error types, supervisory review coverage, and the effect of supervisory review on quality. Missing data elements (per Table 6) include: cases reviewed (performance review), cases with errors and error rates achieved (signatory reviews). Collecting these enables trend analysis and better oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatory Authority Program review procedures and data needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-stage process (partial and full signatory authority) assessing whether examiners are qualified to issue decisions without supervisory review; during both stages supervisors and Technology Center QA specialists review at least 17 decisions per examiner, with each decision reviewed by two panelists and the Technology Center director deciding which errors count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Between FY2012 and mid-FY2014 many examiners received partial/full authority, but USPTO does not systematically collect which decisions contain errors or whether errors are charged during the process. Lack of signatory-review error data prevents verifying examiners' error rates and monitoring trends among senior examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Index and PALM-derived event tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: PALM-derived Quality Index Report tracks events that could indicate quality concerns (e.g., reopened applications, number of determinations per application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supervisors rely heavily on QIR/PALM data to identify potential productivity and quality issues and to target reviews to examiners whose behavior deviates from peers. However, QIR does not track causal reasons for errors; it should be complemented by supervisory review data to monitor trends and root causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: End loading monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitoring the practice of examiners submitting a high volume of written decisions at the end of each quarter (end loading), e.g., percent of examiners who submitted more than half of their work in the last two biweekly periods of a quarter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: End loading may allow meeting production targets while compromising examination quality; OPQA found >150 errors in decisions issued by end loaders. Supervisors and Technology Centers should collect which cases were reviewed and monitor end-loading patterns to detect quality impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent mortgaging detection and disciplinary framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent mortgaging is submitting incomplete work for credit (e.g., to gain awards or avoid warnings); detection tools include administrative return counts and SPE Dashboard metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO treats mortgaging as misconduct, and policies require supervisors to weigh factors when determining discipline (e.g., effect on supervisor confidence in employee's work ability, notoriety/impact on agency reputation, consistency with penalties for similar offenses). The audit found inconsistent responses (ranging from abeyance agreements to suspensions), suggesting a need for consistent controls, monitoring, and penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance appraisal plan effectiveness for measuring quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance appraisal standards (revised FY2011) affect quality ratings and disciplinary actions; evidence shows higher likelihood of commendable/outstanding ratings and very few written warnings for quality compared to production/docket management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A GS-13 examiner with partial signatory authority had an estimated 89% chance of commendable/outstanding under the previous plan and 96% under the FY2011 plan (controlled for other variables), suggesting inflated ratings. Recommendations include refining supervisory guidance, processes, and appraisal plans to better distinguish levels of examiner quality, avoid disincentives for supervisors to charge errors, and ensure meaningful differentiation of outstanding performance.
